sections.html: Synodontis depauwi Boulenger, 1899. Type locality: Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo. Size: 240 mm SL (9.4 inches). FishBase lists 24 cm TL. IUCN Red List category: Least Concern (last assessed 2009).
Africa: Stanley Pool (Congo system), also Lower Congo and Pool Malebo.

Lay the fish in your hand with its head toward your palm and the tail toward your fingers. Hold the dorsal spine between your middle and ring finger so the fish is belly up and you won't be punctured by the sharp fin spines (which hurts - be careful). The genital pore is in a small furrow of tissue (in healthy fish) and is obstructed by the pelvic fins. Pull down on the tail gently to arch the spine and the pelvic fins will stand and the furrow open to display the genital pore and the anus. The male has a somewhat ridged genital papilla on which the spermatoduct is on the back side, facing the tail fin. A gravid female also shows an extended papilla, but the oviduct is on the ventral side of the papilla. It may also show a little redness if gravid. A thin or emaciated female has just two pink pores, the oviduct and the anus.

All species in the genus Synodontis have a hardened head cap attached to a process (humeral process) situated behind the gill opening and pointed towards the posterior. The dorsal and pectoral fins have a hardened, serrated first ray. The caudal fin is always forked. There is one pair of maxillary barbels, sometimes having membranes and occasionally branched. The two pairs of mandibular barbels are often branched and can have nodes. The cone-shaped teeth in the upper jaw are short; those in the lower jaw are S-shaped and movable. These fish produce audible sounds when disturbed by rubbing the base of the pectoral spine against the pectoral girdle.
Annales du Musee du Congo (Ser. Zoology) v. 1 (fasc. 3), pp 45, Pl. 22 (fig. 2).
